_comment: Proposed fixes for Miami Beach and South Beach: shown as the infographic timeline on miami-beach/index.html.
Hand-curated. Review about once a quarter: update status, cost, and outcome, add new projects.
date      YYYY-MM-DD (or YYYY-MM-01 / YYYY-01-01 when only month or year is known)
summary   one or two plain sentences: what it is
status    Planned | In design | In progress | Completed | Revised | On hold
cost      { usd: number, label: text shown on the page }
outcome   what it does or has done, in plain words
sources   at least one { name, url }. Entries without a source are skipped.
inTotal   optional. false = cost is part of a bigger item, so it is left out of the total

items.title: North Beach seawalls and living shorelines
items.summary: New and raised seawalls plus living shoreline (plants and rock) along North Beach waterways.
items.outcome: Recommended for a 50% state cost share in Florida's 2025-26 Resilient Florida plan.

items.title: Indian Creek Drive seawall, 29th to 41st St
items.summary: A new, higher public seawall along Indian Creek Drive, part of the city's program to raise and replace seawalls.
items.outcome: Blocks tidal water from spilling over the bank onto Indian Creek Drive. The city's last update set completion for summer 2023.

items.title: West Avenue Phase II, South Beach
items.summary: Raises West Avenue and Bay Road from 14th Street to Lincoln Road about 24 inches, with a new pump station at 1671 West Ave, new drains, water and sewer lines.
items.outcome: Built to cut rain and high-tide flooding in South Beach's lowest streets. Segments 2 and 3 due spring 2027; the city asked the state for $16.7M more in 2025.

items.title: G.O. Bond: neighborhoods and infrastructure
items.summary: Voters approved a $439M general obligation bond. $198M of it goes to neighborhoods and infrastructure, including flood work.
items.outcome: Issued in parts since 2019. The rest of the bond pays for parks ($169M) and public safety ($72M).

items.title: Indian Creek Drive raised road and pumps
items.summary: A new seawall, permanent pump, and plans to raise Indian Creek Drive, one of the city's worst king tide spots.
items.outcome: During the November 2016 king tide the street stayed dry at high tide, the first big test of the new system.

items.title: Citywide stormwater pumps and raised streets
items.summary: About 60 new stormwater pumps, higher seawalls, and raised roads, starting in South Beach around Alton Road and 10th Street.
items.outcome: First phase largely done by 2016, when the new system kept streets dry during king tides. The city then committed $400M to $500M more to raise low streets.
